_README: Committed-text (readout buffer) space-coalescing parity vectors: a sequence of committer tokens (`emits`) folded left-to-right from an empty buffer through CommittedText.append -> the final buffer (`expected`). Both platform ports run their CommittedText.append and MUST reproduce `expected` exactly. The rule: never a leading space, never two spaces in a row (a single trailing space is kept). The human rationale is docs/adr/0010-committed-text-space-coalescing.md; the upstream emitter is shared/temporal_vectors.json (the committer).
_generated_by: shared/tools/gen_committed_text_vectors.py (uv run). Generated, not hand-edited: the reference append_committed() is re-folded over every authored (emits -> expected) and asserted before writing. Re-run after any change to the buffer space rule.
_rule: Per ADR 0010, the live/incremental analogue of the passage-source sanitiser (ADR 0008): append a SPACE token only when the buffer is non-empty and does not already end in a space; append any non-space token (and "") unchanged. A trailing space is NOT trimmed (it is the in-progress word separator).

_format.cases: Each is {name, emits, expected}. Fold `emits` through CommittedText.append from "" and assert == `expected`.
_format.emits: Ordered committer tokens to append (each a letter, digit, single SPACE, or "").
_format.expected: The resulting buffer string after folding all of `emits`.
_format.name: Human-readable label for debugging. Ignored by the parity harness.
_format._note: Optional human explanation. Ignored by the parity harness.

cases.name: word_no_spaces
cases._note: Letters append verbatim; coalescing only ever touches spaces.

cases.name: digits_are_content
cases._note: A digit is content like a letter -- it can anchor the buffer and reset the space gate.

cases.name: single_leading_space_dropped
cases._note: A held REST before any letter commits a space; the buffer must not start with it.

cases.name: many_leading_spaces_dropped
cases._note: Every leading space is dropped while the buffer is still empty.

cases.name: leading_space_then_letter
cases._note: Leading space dropped; the letter anchors the buffer.

cases.name: letter_then_single_space_kept
cases._note: A trailing word-separator space IS kept (in-progress); only LEADING/DOUBLE spaces go.

cases.name: double_space_coalesces
cases._note: The second space (REST -> space -> indeterminate gap -> REST -> space) coalesces away.

cases.name: word_gap_double_space_coalesces
cases._note: The headline bug: a glitchy rest between words must still yield ONE separator.

cases.name: leading_and_double_space
cases._note: Leading space dropped AND the inter-word double space coalesced, in one fold.

cases.name: space_resets_after_letter
cases._note: A non-space token clears the 'ends in space' state, so the next space is a fresh separator.

cases.name: space_after_coalesce_then_letter
cases._note: Coalesce the double space, then the letter joins after the single surviving space.

cases.name: only_spaces
cases._note: All REST, no content -> empty (never a lone space).

cases.name: empty_token_is_noop
cases._note: "" appends nothing and does not disturb the space gate.
